user_request: Examine https://steel.skild.ai/ and identify useful tasks/mechanisms to borrow for acceptance-focused Robocurve submissions.
priority_basis: Root triage prioritizes reuse that addresses actual rejection mechanisms and can be adapted without replacing the shared runtime. This differs from ranking theoretical solver capabilities.

adoption_priorities.borrow: Contact geometry and SDF convergence tests for real free-part thread engagement.
adoption_priorities.acceptance_value: Addresses failures caused by captive parts or angle-triggered fake fastening.
adoption_priorities.next_step: Retain reusable original-size contact geometry and native SDF authoring pattern. Select a genuinely novel useful task before more simulation. Establish robot grasp, free approach/reengagement and hardware-grounded load requirements; do not rescale M20 evidence to smaller fasteners.
adoption_priorities.limits: Existing example is passive nut motion with mu0.01 and no robot; it is neither a tightening-force calibration nor novel assembly task. Do not transplant its friction estimate as hardware data.
adoption_priorities.completed_step: R2 native contact coupon: 3-turn advance 2.4978 and reverse 2.5016 mm/revolution; free removal and released retention passed. First recontact turn 2.1451 mm/revolution failed ±10% criterion. Later settled fit is exploratory only.

adoption_priorities.borrow: Contact-driven deflecting spring latch, release geometry and pull-back retention checks.
adoption_priorities.acceptance_value: Can improve real connector/clip mechanisms without a positional success snap.
adoption_priorities.next_step: Port only a source-matched useful mechanism to current runtime; validate actual gripper access, spring force and free connector alignment.
adoption_priorities.limits: Example uses gizmo/spring driving, zero-friction connector contacts, unconditional gravity cancellation on plug/latch, and a world-to-plug joint with locked rotation. It demonstrates contact latching under these constraints, not free robot alignment or completion. Plain Ethernet insertion is already a crowded benchmark skill.

adoption_priorities.borrow: Small load-dependent-friction, pinch-torsion and linkage diagnostics.
adoption_priorities.acceptance_value: Expose fake holding/bracing claims before a full build; potentially useful for contour-gauge frame handling and its later real clamp.
adoption_priorities.next_step: Test declared physical material/geometry across load and slip controls, preserving actual actuator limits.
adoption_priorities.limits: Newton coefficient values are not PhysX forces; source parameters need interpretation and hardware support.

adoption_priorities.borrow: Two-way rigid/deformable coupling patterns and deformable material geometry.
adoption_priorities.acceptance_value: Potentially enables faithful cable/cloth interactions where rigid proxies fail.
adoption_priorities.next_step: Separate research track only after a novel task is sourced; fixed materials and actual contact-based grasp/release before adaptation.
adoption_priorities.limits: Higher integration cost. Shirt example changes friction by script phase; nondeterministic grasps and Franka capability do not establish YAM performance. A solver migration would need separate compatibility work and is not required for immediate source reuse.

new_task_leads.name: Ordinary spinning-top launch
new_task_leads.status: no-go after feasibility screen; do not build without new importance and launch evidence

compatibility.existing_runtime: IsaacLab17.0.2 / IsaacSim6.1.0.0 / Warp1.16.0; read-only package inspection
compatibility.sdf_path: Native PhysX SDF512/subgrid6 contact was executed with original-size Factory M20 meshes in isolated coupons, preserving shared runtime. Stable three-turn advance and reverse matched 2.5 mm pitch; no solver migration.

license: Pinned Apache-2.0 project sources downloaded with LICENSE/NOTICE. Individual robot/mesh assets keep separate terms; examples/THIRD_PARTY.md identifies Factory nut/bolt BSD-3-Clause. Preserve matching component notices for any actual reuse.
actions_completed: Executed two isolated original-size native PhysX thread coupons with licenses and source hashes retained.
limitations: STEEL Newton examples were not executed wholesale. Their licensed original-size thread geometry was ported and tested in native PhysX. The diagnostic uses declared compliant COM wrenches, not a robot grasp. First recontact turn failed predeclared lead tolerance; no complete task or fastening-force validation.

additional_task_screen.air_hockey: No new-task clearance: established Robot Air Hockey Challenge overlaps core dynamic striker/puck/goal skill. Steel mallet is wrist-mounted.
additional_task_screen.beer_pong: No new-task clearance: Fancy Gym BeerPong overlaps throw/release/cup capture; physical grip and mandatory bounce alone do not yet establish meaningful novelty.
